source: Google Trends (trends.google.com), worldwide web searches, monthly 2004-01 to 2026-10. Each colour is the search "<colour> nail polish". Batches of five were rescaled to the shared "red nail polish" anchor, then summed by year.
licence: Google Trends data, credited as Source: Google Trends
caveats: Searches, not sales: a colour people are curious about can outrank one they buy.
Trends reports rounded relative interest, so rare colours in early years read as zero.
Google improved its data collection in January 2011, January 2016 and January 2022, which can step a series.
method: Years marked thin have fewer than five colours with 1% of searches, and the page leaves them out. Share is a colour's searches over all 22 colours' searches that year. Colour of the year: the biggest rise in share on the year before, among colours with at least 3% of the year. Palette: the year's top five, with the fifth swapped for the colour of the year when it is not already in.
